tests.title: Test 1 — Data Inspection
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing data. Perform an initial data exploration: number of rows and columns, column names, data types, missing values. Summarize your findings.
tests.model_output: Correct row/column counts (545 x 13), correct dtypes, correctly reports zero missing values. Also mislabels the 'prefarea' column as "str (prefecture/region)" -- the dataset's naming pattern (mainroad, guestroom, basement, hotwaterheating, airconditioning) strongly indicates prefarea is a binary yes/no 'preferred area' flag, not a geographic region.
tests.verdict: PARTIAL -- correct core stats, but a fabricated/incorrect column interpretation, reached only after an extreme retry storm
notes: 83 tool calls (41 exec, 25 write, 17 read) and ~6.2 minutes elapsed before landing on a working script -- extreme trial-and-error even though the eventual output was reasonable.
prefarea mislabeled as 'prefecture/region' -- a fabricated interpretation of a real column, inconsistent with the dataset's own binary-flag naming convention used for every other yes/no column.

Two separate model.completed usage entries logged (484,669 then 2,622,652 tokens) for what was presented as a single-prompt turn -- likely an internal continuation after hitting a length boundary mid-turn, not a second user exchange. Token totals here are summed across both entries.

tests.title: Test 2 — Distribution Analysis
tests.prompt: Analyze the distribution of housing prices. Report: minimum price, maximum price, average price, median price. Explain whether expensive outliers exist.
tests.model_output: No computation attempted -- session shows only a single memory_search call, no read of the CSV, no reported min/max/avg/median price, no outlier discussion.
notes: Cheapest and least-productive session in this set: 1 tool call, 0.0s elapsed, 52,771 tokens -- effectively abandoned after checking memory rather than the actual data file.
Contrasts directly with H01/H04/H05 (similar simple-stats prompts on the numeric housing benchmark), which all completed correctly in a handful of calls -- this session never got that far.

tests.title: Test 3 — Correlation Ranking
tests.prompt: Find which numerical features are most related to house price. Calculate correlations and rank the features.
tests.model_output: No final answer -- session ends mid-loop with no correlation ranking ever produced.
tests.verdict: CRITICAL FAIL -- Type E retry-loop / self-correction spiral
notes: 125 tool calls (74 exec, 48 write, 1 edit, 1 memory_search), ~13.8 minutes, 5,929,228 total tokens -- on a prompt that should be answerable with a single pandas .corr() call.

Transcript shows 50+ consecutive near-identical 'I apologize for all the syntax errors!' restatements, all citing bracket/parenthesis matching issues, without ever escaping via a genuinely different strategy -- same signature as the Type E failures already documented (T4/T8 in the hallucination set).

tests.title: Test 4 — Business Insight
tests.prompt: A real estate company wants to know what property characteristics increase house prices. Analyze the dataset and provide the top drivers of expensive houses.
tests.model_output: Ranked driver table: area/size (highest impact), bathrooms 3+, bedrooms 4+ combined with main-road location, air conditioning, parking+basement -- a plausible, coherent answer, though the rendered table has a garbled duplicated header row.
tests.verdict: PARTIAL -- substantive correct-looking answer, minor presentation/formatting defect
notes: Efficient session: only 7 tool calls, ~2.3 minutes, 238,629 tokens -- far cheaper than the retry-loop sessions while still producing real content.
One of only two sessions in this 8-test set to invoke memory_search (alongside Test3) -- worth checking why, since this is a fresh single-shot session where recalling memory shouldn't be necessary.
The formatting glitch (a malformed double-header markdown table) is a presentation defect distinct from the @tag-format compliance failures seen in H01/H08 -- content itself is not obviously wrong.

tests.title: Test 5 — Categorical Analysis
tests.prompt: Analyze whether furnishing status affects housing price. Calculate average prices by furnishing category and explain the results.
tests.model_output: Transcript excerpt available cuts off right after the model identifies the relevant columns (price, furnishingstatus) -- no furnishing-status price comparison visible in the captured transcript.
tests.verdict: UNCLEAR -- needs verification against raw session
notes: Tool log shows 8 calls (5 write, 2 exec, 1 read) -- more activity than a session that stopped at column identification would need, suggesting the session likely proceeded further than the available transcript excerpt shows.
Recommend checking the raw session transcript directly (not just the paste) before finalizing this verdict -- the extraction data implies more happened than was captured in the provided text.

tests.title: Test 6 — Visualisation Generation
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing price data. Create visualisations showing the main factors affecting house prices. Generate: 1. a price distribution histogram, 2. an area vs price scatter plot, 3. a bar chart of average price by furnishing status. Save each chart as a PNG file in the workspace and explain the key insight from each chart.
tests.model_output: Repeated claims of 'successfully loaded' data and intent to 'run this visualization script', but no PNG files were ultimately produced in the workspace (confirmed by direct inspection).
tests.verdict: CRITICAL FAIL -- Type E retry-loop / self-correction spiral, confirmed zero output
notes: 86 tool calls (42 exec, 34 write, 7 edit, 3 read), ~11.2 minutes, two logged completion rounds totaling ~4.5M tokens.
CONFIRMED by direct workspace inspection: zero PNG files exist despite the transcript's repeated claims of progress -- the session's narrated confidence did not correspond to actual file output.
Only session in this 8-test set to use the edit tool (7 times) -- consistent with repeatedly trying to patch a broken script in place rather than rewriting cleanly from scratch.

tests.title: Test 7 — Full ML Workflow
tests.prompt: The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing market data. Build a machine learning model to predict house prices. Preprocess the categorical variables, split into train/test sets, train a regression model, report evaluation metrics (RMSE and R²), and rank the most important features. Save your model results to a file called model_results.txt in the workspace.
tests.model_output: No confirmed model_results.txt or working model produced -- session ends mid-loop.
tests.verdict: CRITICAL FAIL -- Type E retry-loop / self-correction spiral, most severe in this set
notes: 114 tool calls (58 exec, 49 write, 5 read, 2 process), ~15.5 minutes, 5,882,892 total tokens -- the single most expensive and longest session in this 8-test set.
Longest, most repetitive transcript of all 8 tests -- dozens of near-identical 'Let me try a completely different approach...' restatements, all citing heredoc truncation as the blocker.

Model explicitly self-diagnoses the blocker ('the heredoc keeps getting truncated') dozens of times without ever abandoning that approach for a genuinely different one -- same self-diagnosis-without-adaptation pattern seen in H07.
Uses process (background exec polling) twice -- alongside Test8, the only sessions in this set to do so, consistent with attempting genuine model-training runs rather than pure data exploration.

tests.title: Test 8 — Executive PowerPoint (Email Task)
tests.prompt: You are a data analyst. The file data/housing_dataset.csv contains housing market data. Analyse the dataset end-to-end and create an executive slide deck. The deck should include: dataset overview, important trends, visualisations, key drivers of price, and business recommendations. Save the final presentation as a PowerPoint file called housing_analysis.pptx in the workspace.
tests.model_output: Substantial narrated intention ('Let me create a comprehensive Python script...') but only 8 actual tool calls; no housing_analysis.pptx file exists in the workspace (confirmed by direct inspection).
notes: Only 8 tool calls (3 read, 2 exec, 2 write, 1 process) despite a disproportionately large amount of reasoning text in the transcript -- much of the 'work' described was narrated intention rather than actual tool invocation, a lighter-weight variant of the Type B pattern (reasoning substituting for tool calls) rather than the heavier Type E retry-loop seen in Test3/6/7.
CONFIRMED by direct workspace inspection: no housing_analysis.pptx file exists, consistent with your own observation.
